title: Hodgkin Lymphoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Hodgkin Lymphoma. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (excisional biopsy, CD30/CD15/PAX5/CD20 immunophenotype, whole-body FDG PET-CT, echocardiogram/DLCO PFTs, fertility preservation) -> Histologic Classification (Classical HL vs NLPHL) -> Stage & Risk Stratification (Early Stage I-II Favorable vs Unfavorable vs Advanced Stage III-IV) -> Frontline Advanced cHL with SWOG S1826 Nivolumab + AVD (Category 1 Preferred), ECHELON-1 Brentuximab vedotin + AVD (Category 1 Preferred), RATHL PET-adapted ABVD, and escalated BEACOPP -> Interim PET Response Adaptation (Deauville 1-3 vs 4-5) -> Nodular Lymphocyte-Predominant HL (ISRT, Rituximab, R-CHOP) -> Relapsed/Refractory Salvage (Nivolumab, Brentuximab vedotin, ICE, Gemcitabine, HDT/ASCT). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Hodgkin Lymphoma Version 2.2026 (July 1, 2026).

a.text: Interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles is scored on the 5-point Deauville scale; Deauville 1-3 is treated as a negative (adequate) metabolic response and Deauville 4-5 as positive (inadequate) response. End-of-treatment PET is interpreted the same way to define complete metabolic response.

b.text: Bleomycin carries a risk of cumulative pulmonary toxicity; response-adapted omission after a negative interim PET (continuing as AVD) reduces lung exposure without loss of disease control in the settings where it has been studied. Obtain PFTs with DLCO before bleomycin.

c.text: Discuss fertility preservation (sperm banking / oocyte cryopreservation) before gonadotoxic chemotherapy or pelvic radiation, and counsel on long-term risks (second malignancy, cardiac, thyroid, pulmonary) that drive lifelong survivorship follow-up.

d.text: Escalated BEACOPP achieves high disease control at the cost of greater acute toxicity, infertility, and second-malignancy risk; reserve for selected fit, higher-risk younger patients and weigh explicitly against N-AVD / BV-AVD.

e.text: Brentuximab vedotin causes peripheral sensory neuropathy; avoid with severe preexisting neuropathy and give primary G-CSF prophylaxis with BV-AVD because of a high rate of febrile neutropenia without it.

f.text: For relapsed / refractory classical HL, brentuximab vedotin (CD30-directed) and PD-1 checkpoint inhibitors (nivolumab, pembrolizumab) are active as salvage and post-transplant maintenance (AETHERA, Category 1 for brentuximab vedotin maintenance); a persistently PET-positive site should be re-biopsied to confirm active disease before it is treated as refractory.

nodes.name: Diagnostic workup
nodes.title: Hodgkin lymphoma: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Complete the diagnostic workup before histologic classification and staging. Review each element, then proceed.
bullets: Excisional lymph node biopsy preferred (core biopsy acceptable only if excisional contraindicated; FNA is strictly insufficient for initial diagnosis).
Immunophenotypic panel, Classical HL (cHL): CD30+ (100%), CD15+ (75-85%), PAX5+ (weak), CD20- (or faint heterogeneous <20%), CD45-, CD3-, EBV-LMP1 variable.
Immunophenotypic panel, NLPHL: CD20+ (strong/uniform), CD45+ (LCA), BCL6+, CD79a+, EMA+ (~50%), CD30-, CD15-.
Diagnostic and staging imaging: contrast-enhanced CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis plus whole-body FDG PET-CT (Lugano 2014 criteria; 5-point Deauville scale).
Laboratory baseline: CBC with differential, ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate), CMP (renal and hepatic function), LDH, albumin, HIV, Hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc), Hepatitis C screening.
Pre-chemotherapy organ function: echocardiogram or MUGA (baseline LVEF before anthracycline doxorubicin); pulmonary function tests (PFTs with DLCO before bleomycin).
Reproductive and supportive counseling: sperm banking / oocyte cryopreservation consultation prior to gonadotoxic therapy; psychosocial distress screening.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Histologic Classification

nodes.name: Histologic classification
nodes.title: Hodgkin lymphoma: histology / presentation
nodes.description: Management branches first by histologic subtype and treatment context. Choose the applicable category.
bullets: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL), newly diagnosed: Reed-Sternberg cells with classical immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, weak PAX5).
Nodular lymphocyte-predominant HL (NLPHL): LP (popcorn) cells with retained B-cell program (CD20+, CD45+, BCL6+).
Pediatric / adolescent classical HL: managed on pediatric pathways with age-adapted regimens.
Relapsed or refractory disease after first-line therapy: route to salvage and transplant evaluation.

nodes.name: cHL stage group
nodes.title: Classical HL: Ann Arbor stage group
nodes.description: Split into early stage (I-II) and advanced stage (III-IV) disease; early stage is further stratified by favorable vs unfavorable risk factors.

tables.title: Ann Arbor / Lugano stage (simplified)
rows: Single nodal region or single extranodal site
Two or more nodal regions, same side of the diaphragm
Nodal regions on both sides of the diaphragm
Diffuse extranodal involvement (e.g. liver, marrow, lung)

nodes.name: Early risk group
nodes.title: Early-stage cHL: favorable vs unfavorable
nodes.description: Any listed adverse factor moves early-stage disease from favorable to unfavorable and intensifies therapy.
bullets: B-symptoms present (fever, drenching night sweats, weight loss).
Bulky mass: 10 cm or greater, or greater than one-third of the transthoracic diameter on chest imaging.
Three or more involved nodal sites.
ESR 50 or greater, or ESR 30 or greater with B-symptoms.

nodes.name: Early favorable interim PET
nodes.title: Early favorable cHL: ABVD x2, then interim PET
nodes.description: Start ABVD for 2 cycles, then reassess with interim FDG-PET and adapt by Deauville response.
nodes.path: Hodgkin Lymphoma / cHL / Early favorable / Interim PET
bullets: Give ABVD x2 cycles, then interim FDG-PET scored by Deauville.
Deauville 1-2 (negative): consolidate with ISRT 20 Gy, or give ABVD x1 additional cycle (chemotherapy-alone strategy).
Deauville 3-5 (positive): escalate therapy and add involved-site RT.

nodes.name: Early favorable PET-negative
nodes.title: Early favorable, PET-negative: ISRT 20 Gy or ABVD x1
nodes.description: Negative interim PET after ABVD x2; consolidate with low-dose radiation or one additional ABVD cycle.
nodes.path: Hodgkin Lymphoma / cHL / Early favorable / PET-negative
bullets: Deauville 1-2 after ABVD x2 confirms an adequate metabolic response.
Consolidate with ISRT 20 Gy (combined-modality), or give ABVD x1 additional cycle if sparing radiation.
Consider bleomycin omission in later cycles to reduce pulmonary toxicity.
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET before declaring remission; then survivorship surveillance.

nodes.name: Early favorable PET-positive
nodes.title: Early favorable, PET-positive: escalate therapy
nodes.description: Inadequate interim response; escalate chemotherapy and add involved-site radiation.
nodes.path: Hodgkin Lymphoma / cHL / Early favorable / PET-positive
bullets: Deauville 3-5 after ABVD x2: escalate (complete full ABVD course, or escalated BEACOPP in fit patients, or BV-AVD).
Add involved-site RT to residual / bulky sites.
Re-biopsy a persistently PET-positive site to exclude refractory disease before declaring failure.
If biopsy confirms refractory disease, enter the relapsed / refractory pathway; otherwise proceed to surveillance.

nodes.name: Early unfavorable treatment
nodes.title: Early unfavorable cHL: ABVD x4 or BV-AVD x4, plus or minus ISRT
nodes.description: Unfavorable early-stage disease receives more chemotherapy, with radiation to bulk or residual sites.
nodes.path: Hodgkin Lymphoma / cHL / Early unfavorable / Treatment
bullets: Give ABVD x4 cycles with or without ISRT 30 Gy to bulky / residual sites.
Alternative: BV-AVD x4 cycles with or without ISRT (requires primary G-CSF prophylaxis; avoid with severe preexisting neuropathy).
Reassess with interim and end-of-treatment FDG-PET (Deauville) and re-biopsy persistent PET-positive sites.
Then survivorship surveillance if complete metabolic response is documented.

nodes.name: Advanced frontline choice
nodes.title: Advanced-stage cHL: choose frontline strategy
nodes.description: Three NCCN frontline options for advanced classical HL. Select the strategy that fits age, comorbidity, and patient preference.
bullets: SWOG S1826, Nivolumab + AVD (N-AVD x6): Category 1 Preferred for age 12 and above; superior PFS (94% vs 86% at 1 year) with lower toxicity (no neuropathy, no bleomycin pneumonitis).
ECHELON-1, Brentuximab vedotin + AVD (BV-AVD x6): Category 1 Preferred with an overall survival advantage over ABVD; requires primary G-CSF prophylaxis; avoid with severe preexisting neuropathy.
RATHL, ABVD with interim PET-2 response adaptation: ABVD x2, then omit bleomycin if PET-negative or escalate if PET-positive.

options.label: SWOG S1826: Nivolumab + AVD x6 (Category 1 Preferred)
ECHELON-1: Brentuximab vedotin + AVD x6 (Category 1 Preferred)

nodes.name: Advanced N-AVD
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: Nivolumab + AVD x6 (SWOG S1826)
nodes.description: Category 1 Preferred frontline for advanced cHL, age 12 and above.
bullets: Give Nivolumab + AVD x6 cycles (SWOG S1826), Category 1 Preferred for age 12 and above.
Superior PFS over BV-AVD (94% vs 86% at 1 year) with lower toxicity: no peripheral neuropathy and no bleomycin pneumonitis.
Monitor for immune-related adverse events (thyroid, colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis) throughout therapy.
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET; re-biopsy persistent PET-positive sites before declaring refractory disease.

nodes.name: Advanced BV-AVD
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: Brentuximab vedotin + AVD x6 (ECHELON-1)
nodes.description: Category 1 Preferred frontline with an overall survival advantage over ABVD.
bullets: Give Brentuximab vedotin + AVD x6 cycles (ECHELON-1), Category 1 Preferred for advanced cHL.
Overall survival advantage over ABVD; give primary G-CSF prophylaxis with every cycle.
Avoid with severe preexisting neuropathy; dose-modify for emerging sensory neuropathy.
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET; re-biopsy persistent PET-positive sites before declaring refractory disease.

nodes.name: RATHL interim PET-2
nodes.title: RATHL: ABVD x2, then interim PET-2
nodes.description: Start ABVD for 2 cycles, then adapt by interim PET-2 Deauville score.
nodes.path: Hodgkin Lymphoma / cHL / Advanced / RATHL / Interim PET
bullets: Give ABVD x2 cycles, then interim FDG-PET (PET-2) scored by Deauville.
Deauville 1-3 (negative): omit bleomycin and continue AVD x4 cycles (total 6 cycles).
Deauville 4-5 (positive): escalate to escalated BEACOPP x4 cycles or BV-AVD.

nodes.name: RATHL PET-negative
nodes.title: RATHL PET-negative: omit bleomycin, AVD x4
nodes.description: Negative interim PET-2; de-escalate to AVD to spare bleomycin lung toxicity.
nodes.path: Hodgkin Lymphoma / cHL / Advanced / RATHL / PET-negative
bullets: Deauville 1-3 on PET-2: omit bleomycin and continue AVD x4 cycles (total 6 cycles).
De-escalation preserves disease control while reducing bleomycin pulmonary toxicity.
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET; re-biopsy persistent PET-positive sites before declaring refractory disease.

nodes.name: RATHL PET-positive
nodes.title: RATHL PET-positive: escalate to escalated BEACOPP or BV-AVD
nodes.description: Positive interim PET-2; escalate to intensified therapy.
nodes.path: Hodgkin Lymphoma / cHL / Advanced / RATHL / PET-positive
bullets: Deauville 4-5 on PET-2: escalate to escalated BEACOPP x4 cycles, or switch to BV-AVD.
Reserve escalated BEACOPP for fit younger patients after explicit counseling on infertility and second-malignancy risk.
BV-AVD escalation requires primary G-CSF prophylaxis.
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET; re-biopsy persistent PET-positive sites before declaring refractory disease.

nodes.name: NLPHL stage group
nodes.title: NLPHL: stage and symptom group
nodes.description: NLPHL management depends on stage, bulk, and symptoms. Select the applicable group.
bullets: Stage IA / IIA non-bulky without symptoms: localized disease amenable to radiation or surveillance.
Stage IB / IIB / III / IV or symptomatic / bulky disease: systemic therapy required.

options.label: Stage IB / IIB / III / IV, bulky, or symptomatic

nodes.name: NLPHL early treatment
nodes.title: NLPHL stage IA / IIA: ISRT 30 Gy or surveillance
nodes.description: Localized NLPHL is controlled with involved-site radiation or observed after complete excision.
bullets: Give involved-site RT (ISRT 30 Gy) to the involved field for stage IA / IIA non-bulky disease.
Active surveillance is acceptable if the involved node was completely excised.
Follow long term: NLPHL can relapse late and carries a risk of transformation to aggressive B-cell lymphoma (re-biopsy new growth).

nodes.name: NLPHL advanced treatment
nodes.title: NLPHL advanced / symptomatic: Rituximab-based systemic therapy
nodes.description: CD20-positive NLPHL responds to rituximab alone or rituximab plus chemotherapy.
bullets: Rituximab monotherapy for low-burden or frail patients.
Rituximab + CHOP (R-CHOP) for bulky or high-burden disease.
Alternatives: rituximab + CVP, or rituximab + AVD in selected patients.
Re-biopsy suspected transformation; transformed disease is treated as aggressive B-cell lymphoma.

nodes.name: Pediatric treatment
nodes.title: Pediatric / adolescent cHL: pediatric protocol therapy
nodes.description: Children and adolescents are treated on age-adapted pediatric regimens under pediatric oncology care.
bullets: Refer to a pediatric oncology center; manage on the StewardMD pediatric Hodgkin protocol (ABVE-PC backbone, response-adapted).
Complete pediatric staging workup including growth, puberty, cardiac, and fertility baselines before therapy.
Use response-adapted radiation sparing per the pediatric protocol to limit late effects.
Long-term survivorship follow-up for growth, fertility, cardiac, and second-malignancy surveillance.

nodes.name: Relapse context
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory cHL: transplant history
nodes.description: Salvage strategy depends on whether the patient has already received high-dose therapy with autologous transplant.
bullets: No prior ASCT and fit for transplant: give salvage therapy, then consolidate chemosensitive response with HDT/ASCT.
Relapse after ASCT: move to post-transplant maintenance and sequential novel agents.

options.label: No prior ASCT, candidate for salvage plus transplant

nodes.name: Salvage regimen choice
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory cHL: choose salvage regimen
nodes.description: Checkpoint inhibitor-based and CD30-directed salvage options. Select the regimen that fits prior exposure and comorbidity.
bullets: Checkpoint inhibitor-based salvage: nivolumab combined with ICE chemotherapy.
Pembrolizumab monotherapy is an alternative checkpoint option (carried as written guidance).
CD30-directed salvage: brentuximab vedotin-based therapy.
Gemcitabine-based salvage combinations for patients needing non-cross-resistant chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Salvage Nivo-ICE
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: Nivolumab + ICE salvage
nodes.description: Checkpoint inhibitor combined with ICE salvage chemotherapy, then transplant consolidation for responders.
bullets: Give nivolumab combined with ICE salvage chemotherapy.
Reassess with FDG-PET after salvage; chemosensitive response proceeds to HDT/ASCT (next step).
Monitor for immune-related adverse events alongside ICE cytopenias.
nodes.linkLabel: Responders: proceed to high-dose therapy with autologous transplant

nodes.name: Salvage BV
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: Brentuximab vedotin salvage
nodes.description: CD30-directed salvage for relapsed / refractory classical HL, then transplant consolidation for responders.
bullets: Give brentuximab vedotin-based salvage therapy.
Reassess with FDG-PET after salvage; chemosensitive response proceeds to HDT/ASCT (next step).
Monitor for peripheral neuropathy and neutropenia.
nodes.linkLabel: Responders: proceed to high-dose therapy with autologous transplant

nodes.name: Salvage gemcitabine
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: Gemcitabine-based salvage
nodes.description: Gemcitabine-based salvage combinations, then transplant consolidation for responders.
bullets: Give gemcitabine-based salvage chemotherapy.
Reassess with FDG-PET after salvage; chemosensitive response proceeds to HDT/ASCT (next step).
Consider for patients needing non-cross-resistant chemotherapy after prior anthracycline exposure.
nodes.linkLabel: Responders: proceed to high-dose therapy with autologous transplant

nodes.name: HDT-ASCT consolidation
nodes.title: Chemosensitive response: HDT with autologous transplant
nodes.description: Consolidate chemosensitive salvage response with high-dose therapy and autologous stem cell transplantation.
bullets: Chemosensitive response to salvage proceeds to high-dose therapy with autologous stem cell transplantation (HDT/ASCT).
Collect stem cells before myeloablative conditioning; confirm adequate organ function and performance status.
After ASCT, assess recurrence risk: high-risk patients proceed to post-ASCT maintenance.

nodes.name: Post-ASCT maintenance
nodes.title: Post-ASCT: Brentuximab vedotin or Pembrolizumab maintenance
nodes.description: Maintenance for high recurrence risk after autologous transplant.
bullets: Brentuximab vedotin maintenance for high recurrence risk after ASCT (AETHERA, Category 1).
Pembrolizumab maintenance is an alternative for high-risk patients (carried as written guidance).
Monitor for peripheral neuropathy on brentuximab vedotin and immune-related adverse events on pembrolizumab.
